items.stem: Which statement best describes 'augmented reality (AR)'?
options: A database in CAT software that stores sentences already translated so they can be reused.
Technology that overlays computer-generated images or information on a live view of the real world, e.g. through a phone camera.
Using storage, processing and software provided over the internet by a third party, usually paid for as it is used, instead of on local hardware.
The proportion of attempts by unauthorised people that a biometric system wrongly accepts.
items.answer: Technology that overlays computer-generated images or information on a live view of the real world, e.g. through a phone camera.
items.markingKey: augmented reality (AR): Technology that overlays computer-generated images or information on a live view of the real world, e.g. through a phone camera.

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'execution stage' and 'monitoring and control'.
items.answer: execution stage: The stage in which the planned tasks are carried out and the product or system is built. monitoring and control: Checking progress against the plan throughout the project and taking action if tasks are late or over budget.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: execution stage correctly described; 1 mark: monitoring and control correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Isla is preparing a targeted mailing for MetroBus in Dhaka. Evaluate the use of filters and IF fields to personalise mailings from MetroBus.
items.answer: Points for: relevant messages; better response; fewer wasted letters. Points against / limitations: complex rules can contain errors; relies on accurate data; customers may feel profiled. Conclusion: well-tested filters and IF fields improve targeting; rules must be checked with test merges.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: relevant messages; better response; fewer wasted letters. Against: complex rules can contain errors; relies on accurate data; customers may feel profiled. Conclusion may argue: well-tested filters and IF fields improve targeting; rules must be checked with test merges. [6]

items.stem: Chloe is planning the network for a new branch of Delta Water Utility in Accra. (a) Describe what is meant by a WLAN. (b) Explain why staff working from home should use a VPN. (c) Describe one use of a WPAN by staff.
items.answer: (a) A local network where devices connect wirelessly through access points. (b) Encrypted tunnel protects data over the internet; access to internal resources as if in the office. (c) Bluetooth headset with phone; smart watch notifications; wireless keyboard/mouse.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark local; 1 mark wireless/access points. [2] (b) 1 mark each. [2] (c) 1 mark use; 1 mark description. [2]

items.stem: Samuel is a knowledge engineer working for Starlight Cinemas in Santiago. (a) Describe how knowledge is gathered from experts. (b) Evaluate the difficulties Starlight Cinemas may face in creating an expert system.
items.answer: (a) Interviews; observation of experts at work; questionnaires; studying manuals and case records. (b) For: experts may struggle to explain intuitive knowledge; experts may disagree; time and cost; knowledge changes. Against: once built, the system captures expertise permanently and gives consistent advice; benefits may outweigh costs. Conclusion: the system is worthwhile if experts are committed and it is maintained.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per method, max 2. [2] (b) Up to 3 marks for points on each side applied to the scenario; 1 further mark requires a justified conclusion. [6]

items.stem: Zara, the IT manager at Vista Estate Agents in Seoul, is writing a report on cloud computing, IoT sensors and 3D printing for the directors. Evaluate whether Vista Estate Agents should move all its data and software to the cloud.
items.answer: Points for: lower capital cost; scalability; remote access; provider handles backup and security updates. Points against / limitations: internet dependence; privacy and legal concerns; ongoing costs; vendor lock-in; less control. Conclusion: a hybrid approach keeps sensitive data local while using the cloud for scalable services.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: lower capital cost; scalability; remote access; provider handles backup and security updates. Against: internet dependence; privacy and legal concerns; ongoing costs; vendor lock-in; less control. Conclusion may argue: a hybrid approach keeps sensitive data local while using the cloud for scalable services. [6]

items.stem: The security services in Toronto have asked Vista Estate Agents to analyse travel and communication data. (a) Explain what is meant by data mining. (b) Describe two ways the organisation could use data mining. (c) Explain why the results of data mining should be checked by experts.
items.answer: (a) Analysing large data sets with software to find hidden patterns and relationships. (b) Market-basket analysis; predicting demand; fraud detection; identifying risk factors; customer segmentation; detecting suspicious behaviour. (c) Patterns may be coincidental or correlations may not be causes; decisions need human judgement.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark large data; 1 mark hidden patterns. [2] (b) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (c) 1 mark correlation not causation; 1 mark human judgement. [2]

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'wireless access point (WAP)'?

items.markingKey: wireless access point (WAP): A device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network using Wi-Fi.

items.stem: Palm Grove Hotel in Karachi needs a new logo and product photographs for its website. (a) Explain why the logo should be created as a vector graphic. (b) Describe the difference between lossy and lossless compression. (c) Recommend a file format for the product photographs and justify your choice. (d) Explain what happens to a bitmap image when it is enlarged.
items.answer: (a) Scales to any size (business card to billboard) without losing quality; editable objects; small file. (b) Lossy permanently removes data for smaller files; lossless reduces size with no data lost. (c) JPEG — small files via lossy compression, good for photos. (d) Pixels are enlarged/interpolated so the image becomes blocky or blurred (pixelation).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark each. [2] (c) 1 mark format; 1 mark justification. [2] (d) 1 mark pixels enlarged; 1 mark pixelation. [2]

items.stem: Tariq manages the network at FreshFarm Foods in Santiago, where staff use the internet every day. Evaluate whether a firewall and a proxy server are enough to keep the network of FreshFarm Foods secure.
items.answer: Points for: block unauthorised traffic; filter sites; hide addresses; log activity. Points against / limitations: insider threats; phishing and malware via allowed traffic; encrypted traffic is harder to inspect; misconfiguration. Conclusion: they are essential layers but must be combined with encryption, anti-malware, updates and training.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. items.stem: Which statement best describes 'knowledge base'?

The part of an expert system that stores facts about the subject area, collected from human experts.

items.stem: Which statement best describes 'animation layer'?

A separate track on the timeline holding one object or group, so it can be animated independently of others.

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'latency' and 'geostationary satellite'.

items.stem: Coral Bay Aquarium in Accra is building an expert system for car fault diagnosis. An expert says: "If engine will not start and lights are dim, then battery is flat." (a) Write this knowledge as a rule for the rules base. (b) Explain how the inference engine would use this rule in forward chaining. (c) Describe how the knowledge engineer would check that the rule is correct.
items.answer: (a) IF engine will not start AND lights are dim THEN battery is flat (b) When all conditions are in the known facts, the rule fires and "battery is flat" is added as a new fact, which may allow further rules to fire. (c) Discuss with experts, test with real cases and compare the system's conclusions with experts' decisions.
items.markingKey: (a) correct IF ... AND ... THEN form [2] (b) conditions matched against facts; rule fires; new fact added; may trigger other rules [2] (c) checked with experts / tested on cases with known outcomes [2]. [6]
